lessons.title: Your capstone: batch record, safety report and 90-day plan
objectives: Assemble a complete capstone evidence pack
Write a short safety report on your own process
Plan 90 days of production around curing time
Set measurable sales and quality targets for the next quarter

blocks.text: This lesson brings everything together. Your capstone proves you can make a safe, correctly calculated, cured and honestly labelled soap, know what it costs, and have a realistic plan to sell it. It is also the starting file for your NAFDAC readiness and for any buyer or partner who asks how you work.

blocks.name: business-plan
blocks.alt: A woman presenting a business plan chart
blocks.caption: Your 90-day plan schedules batches ahead of sales by at least the curing time.

blocks.text: What goes in your capstone pack

items: **Recipe and calculation:** your oil percentages and grams, the hand calculation of caustic soda and water, and the matching SoapCalc screenshot.
**Batch record:** times, temperatures, trace time, bars cut, weekly cure weights, pH result.
**Photo evidence:** safety setup, the poured mould, cut bars curing, finished labelled bar.
**Quality checklist:** each fault from Lesson 3.1 checked as present or absent, and your sell or discard decision.
**Costing sheet:** full cost per good bar and your retail and wholesale prices.
**Safety report and reflection:** see below.
**90-day plan.**

blocks.text: Writing your safety report

Keep it to one page. Describe your workspace and how you keep children and others away. List your protective equipment. Explain how you mix lye and in what order. Write your first aid steps. Record any near-miss honestly, for example a splash on the table or a moment you forgot goggles, and what you changed. A safety report that admits a near-miss and fixes it is stronger than one that claims nothing ever happens.
Getting useful feedback

Give two or three cured bars to people who will be honest with you, such as a neighbour, a hairdresser or a friend with sensitive skin. Ask them to use the soap for a week, then ask specific questions: How long did the bar last? Did it lather well in your water? Did your skin feel tight, itchy or fine? Did you like the smell? Would you pay 2,000 naira for it? Write their answers down word for word. Specific questions get useful answers; "Do you like it?" only gets politeness.
Planning around curing time

Because cold-process bars cure for 4 to 6 weeks, soap you want to sell in month two must be made in month one. Plan production in waves: make a batch every week or two so you always have bars curing and bars ready. Feedback also lags: you will only know how customers like a batch after it has cured and been used.

blocks.title: A 90-day starter plan
items: Days 1 to 14: two test batches
Days 15 to 30: CAC, labels, costing
Days 31 to 60: first sales
Days 61 to 90: grow and review
blocks.caption: Production runs ahead of sales by at least the curing time.

blocks.title: Worked example: a 90-day plan with numbers
blocks.context: For example, Ngozi in Enugu finishes the course with one good test batch and wants to sell 60 bars in her first 90 days at 2,000 naira each (approximate).
steps: Days 1 to 14: makes two more batches of 10 bars (weeks 1 and 2), each with a batch record.
Days 15 to 30: registers her business name with CAC, prints labels, confirms her costing at 1,200 naira per bar. Makes batch 4.
Days 31 to 60: first two batches are cured. Sells 25 bars through WhatsApp and her church group. Makes batches 5 and 6.
Days 61 to 90: sells 35 more bars, including 10 at wholesale (1,600 naira) to one salon. Total 60 bars.
Revenue: 50 x 2,000 + 10 x 1,600 = 116,000 naira. Cost: 60 x 1,200 = 72,000 naira. Profit after paying herself for labour: 44,000 naira (approximate).
blocks.result: Ngozi has clear monthly targets, a production schedule that respects curing time, and numbers she can check against her records at day 90.

blocks.text: Before you submit

items: Check every calculation once more against SoapCalc.
Confirm every photo is clear and labelled with the batch number.
Write a short reflection: what changed after feedback from at least two people who used your soap.
Complete the final quiz; you need at least 70% for the certificate.

blocks.text: After day 90, compare your real numbers with the plan. If you sold fewer bars than planned, look at your sales notebook: which channel worked, which did not, and what customers said. If you sold out early, increase batch size or frequency, and remember to plan for the extra caustic soda, oils and curing space. Then write your next 90-day plan. Possible next steps include completing NAFDAC registration, adding a liquid wash line, or training a helper using your batch records.

blocks.title: Honest evidence only
blocks.text: Submit your own photos and numbers, even if a batch failed. A failed batch with a clear diagnosis and fix shows more skill than borrowed pictures.

takeaways: The capstone proves safety, correct calculation, quality, costing and a plan
A good safety report names near-misses and the fixes
Production must run ahead of sales by the curing time
Set measurable 90-day targets for bars, revenue and profit

activity.title: Draft your 90-day plan
steps: Write your sales target in bars and naira for the next 90 days.
Work backwards to schedule batches, allowing 4 to 6 weeks of cure.
List three tasks for each month (for example CAC registration, labels, one new shop).
Choose two numbers you will check at day 90 (for example bars sold and reject rate).
activity.evidence: Your one-page 90-day plan with dates, batch schedule and targets.

quiz.q: A batch costs 8,800 naira before labour and gives 11 good bars. What is the cost per bar before labour?
quiz.explain: 8,800 / 11 = 800 naira per good bar. Always divide by good bars, not bars cut.

quiz.q: Full cost per bar is 1,500 naira and Zainab wants a 40% margin. What price should she set?
A customer sends a screenshot showing a transfer, but nothing shows in Uche's Moniepoint app yet. What should she do?
options: Wait until the money appears in her own app before sending the soap
Send the soap, the screenshot is proof
Ask for the customer's PIN to check
quiz.explain: Screenshots and SMS alerts can be faked. Release goods only after confirming in your own account.

quiz.q: Ngozi wants bars to sell at a fair 6 weeks from today. When must she make them?
options: Within the next few days, to allow 4 to 6 weeks of curing
quiz.explain: Cold-process bars need 4 to 6 weeks to cure, so production must start now.

quiz.q: Equipment cost 24,000 naira and profit per bar is 600 naira. How many bars must she sell to break even on equipment?

finalQuiz.q: What two ingredients react to make true bar soap?
options: Palm oil and soda ash only
finalQuiz.explain: Saponification is the reaction of fats or oils with lye. For bars the lye is sodium hydroxide.

finalQuiz.q: Which is the correct way to make a lye solution?
options: Add water to caustic soda in a closed kitchen
Mix caustic soda with hot oil
Slowly add caustic soda to cold water in a ventilated place, wearing goggles and gloves
Dissolve caustic soda in an aluminium pot
finalQuiz.explain: Caustic soda goes into water, slowly, with ventilation and protective equipment. Aluminium reacts with lye.

finalQuiz.q: Lye solution splashes into Aisha's eye. What is the right response?
options: Rinse with clean running water for at least 15 minutes and go to hospital
Wait to see if it stings
finalQuiz.explain: Eyes need immediate, prolonged rinsing and urgent medical care.

finalQuiz.q: Shea butter has a SAP value of 0.128. How much caustic soda do 200 g of shea butter need at 0% superfat?
A recipe needs 150 g of caustic soda at 0% superfat. How much water is needed at a 33% lye concentration, after a 5% superfat?
finalQuiz.explain: Lye at 5% superfat: 150 x 0.95 = 142.5 g. Water: 142.5 / 0.33 = 431.8, minus 142.5 = about 289 g.

finalQuiz.q: Why do soap makers use a superfat?
options: To leave a little unreacted oil as a safety margin and make the bar milder
finalQuiz.explain: Superfat means slightly less lye than needed, so no free lye remains.

finalQuiz.q: Which product is usually a liquid detergent rather than true soap?
options: Coconut oil and potassium hydroxide paste diluted with water
Keg dish wash made from SLES, water and salt
finalQuiz.explain: SLES is a synthetic cleaning agent. True liquid soap is made from oils and potassium hydroxide.

finalQuiz.q: Bars were cut 2 weeks ago and a buyer wants them today. What should Bisi do?
options: Sell them now at full price
Explain they need 4 to 6 weeks of cure and offer a date
Wrap them in nylon to speed up curing
finalQuiz.explain: Cold-process soap needs 4 to 6 weeks to harden and become milder. Nylon traps moisture.

finalQuiz.q: A finished bar tests clearly above pH 10 and stings the skin. What does it suggest?
options: Excess lye; do not sell and check the calculation
finalQuiz.explain: Handmade soap usually tests about pH 9 to 10. Clearly higher with stinging suggests excess lye.

finalQuiz.q: Which label wording is acceptable for a soap?
options: Made with palm kernel oil and shea butter, net weight 120 g
finalQuiz.explain: Honest ingredient and weight information is fine. Treatment claims are medicinal and "chemical free" is untrue.

finalQuiz.q: Under NAFDAC's MSME route, which statement is correct?
options: Soap does not need any NAFDAC registration
Micro-scale applicants can register unlimited products
Micro businesses (fewer than 10 employees) can register soaps, with evidence of a CAC business name
Registration is done only through private agents
finalQuiz.explain: NAFDAC's MSME page lists soaps among micro-scale products, accepts business name registration for MSMEs, and limits micro scale to five products.

finalQuiz.q: A batch costs 10,800 naira including labour and gives 12 good bars. Using a 40% margin, what retail price should Amaka set?
finalQuiz.explain: Cost per bar: 10,800 / 12 = 900 naira. Price: 900 / 0.60 = 1,500 naira.

capstone.title: Soap batch record and safety report
capstone.brief: Make one full cold-process batch from a recipe you calculated yourself, cure and test it, and submit an evidence pack: recipe and lye calculation with SoapCalc check, batch record, photos, quality checklist, costing sheet, one-page safety report, reflection on feedback, and a 90-day plan.
steps: Design a four-oil recipe and calculate caustic soda (5% superfat) and water (about 33% lye concentration) by hand; confirm it in SoapCalc.
Set up your safety station and make the batch, recording weights, temperatures and trace time.
Cut, cure for at least 4 weeks, weigh three marked bars weekly and test pH.
Complete the quality checklist and decide sell, use or discard.
Label a finished bar honestly and complete a costing sheet with retail and wholesale prices.
Give bars to at least two people, collect specific feedback and write a short reflection.
Write a one-page safety report and a 90-day production and sales plan.

Photos: safety setup, poured mould, curing bars, labelled finished bar
Weekly cure weights and pH strip photo
Quality checklist with sell or discard decision
